beats.intro: Module seven. [[sub]]Yield measures, compounding conventions, and yield spreads.
beats.period: A bond's annual yield depends on how often interest is compounded. [[a]]The number of periods per year is the periodicity. A bond with semiannual coupons and a stated yield of three point two percent has a periodicity of two: one point six percent, twice a year. [[b]]All else equal, more frequent compounding earns more. Take a stated rate of five percent. [[bars]]Compounded annually, the effective annual rate is five percent. Semiannually, five point oh six two five. Quarterly, five point oh nine four five. Monthly, five point one one six two. [[c]]The effective annual rate has a periodicity of one.
beats.convert: So the same return can be stated at different rates, depending on the periodicity. [[z]]Take a five year zero-coupon bond priced at eighty. Stated with annual compounding, its yield is four point five six four percent. Semiannual, four point five one three. Quarterly, four point four eight eight. Monthly, four point four seven one. [[rule]]The rule: compounding more often goes with a lower stated rate. [[f]]To convert, the growth over a year must match. One plus the annual rate over m, to the power m, equals one plus the annual rate over n, to the power n. [[ex]]A three year, five percent semiannual bond priced at one hundred four has a semiannual bond basis yield of three point five eight two percent. Quarterly, that is three point five six six. Monthly, three point five five six.
beats.strips: Strip bonds make a clean comparison. [[a]]A strip is a single coupon or principal payment, separated from a bond, and sold as a zero-coupon bond. [[b]]Take a twenty year Canadian strip priced at sixty nine point four three. Its effective annual yield is one point eight four one percent. [[c]]Converted to a semiannual bond basis, one point eight three three. [[d]]A new twenty year coupon bond yields one point eight eight oh. To compare, both must use the same periodicity.
beats.yields: Other yield measures. [[cy]]Current yield is the annual coupon divided by the flat price. A three point two percent bond priced at ninety eight point seven has a current yield of three point two four two percent. [[crude]]It is crude. It ignores interest on interest, and any gain or loss as the price moves to par. [[street]]Another is the street convention. It assumes cash flows arrive on their scheduled dates, even when one falls on a weekend or holiday. [[simple]]And simple yield adds the coupons and the straight-line gain or loss, divided by the flat price.
beats.options: A callable bond has more yields to consider. [[ytc]]Yield to call assumes the issuer calls on a call date, at the call price. [[ytw]]The yield to worst is the lowest of all the yields to call and the yield to maturity. For the VIVU bond, the yield to first call is five point one five percent, below the yield to maturity of five point three seven. So the yield to worst is five point one five. [[oas]]A more precise way values the call option with a pricing model. The option value is the price of the option-free bond minus the price of the callable bond. Adding it to the flat price gives the option-adjusted price, and from it the option-adjusted yield.
beats.spreads: A yield can be split into a benchmark rate and a spread. [[top]]The benchmark reflects top-down conditions that affect all bonds. [[bot]]The spread reflects bottom-up factors for this issuer: credit risk, liquidity, and taxation. [[g]]The G-spread is the bond's yield minus a government bond yield of the same maturity. If there is no matching government bond, interpolate between the two nearest. [[ex]]For example, a bond yields three point seven five six percent. Interpolating government yields gives two point one oh percent. The G-spread is one point six five six percent, or one hundred sixty six basis points.
beats.zspread: Two more spreads. [[i]]The I-spread is the yield minus the swap rate of the same tenor. It is common for euro corporate bonds, and issuers use it to compare fixed and floating borrowing. [[z]]The Z-spread is different. It is the constant spread added to every point on the benchmark spot curve, so that the present value of the bond's cash flows equals its price. [[oas]]The option-adjusted spread is the Z-spread, adjusted for the value of an embedded call option. [[ex]]For one corporate bond, the G-spread was seventy six basis points, the I-spread one hundred six, and the Z-spread one hundred nine. Analysts track these spreads against their history, to judge whether a bond looks cheap or expensive.
beats.wrap: Let's recap. [[w1]]More frequent compounding means a lower stated rate for the same return. [[w2]]Convert between periodicities, so that yields are comparable. [[w3]]A callable bond is judged by its yield to worst, or option-adjusted yield. [[w4]]Spreads over a benchmark: G-spread, I-spread, Z-spread, and option-adjusted spread.
